source_changes.old_Statement: For $n=2$ or $3$, let $X=\mathbb P^n_{\mathbb C}$ and let $X^{an}$ be its complex analytic space and $\eta:X^{an}\to X$ the canonical morphism of ringed spaces. Define analytification on $X^{an}$ by $\mathcal F^{an}=\eta^{-1}\mathcal F\otimes_{\eta^{-1}\mathcal O_X}\mathcal O_{X^{an}}$. It is an exact tensor-compatible equivalence from algebraic coherent sheaves (locally finitely presented $\mathcal O_X$-modules) to holomorphic coherent sheaves. It identifies algebraic and holomorphic morphisms, preserves cohomology and the derived morphism groups $\operatorname{Ext}^q$, and commutes with restriction to the fixed hyperplane $L_\infty=\{z_0=0\}$. For an algebraic coherent sheaf $\mathcal E$ flat over a finite-type complex parameter scheme $S$, let $p:X\times S\to S$ be projection. Analytification commutes with the algebraic family structure and fiber restrictions. Whenever the algebraic and analytic higher direct images $R^qp_*\mathcal E$ are locally free and the natural maps from their residue-field fibers to $H^q(X_s,\mathcal E_s)$ are isomorphisms, the comparison identifies those direct images and base-change maps. No assertion is made that an arbitrary holomorphic family over a nonproper algebraic base algebraizes.

source_changes.old_Statement:
Assume AC. Let $L_\infty=\{z_0=0\}\subset\mathbb P^2_{\mathbb C}$ and let $\mathcal E$ be an algebraic coherent sheaf (a locally finitely presented module over the structure sheaf) of generic rank $N\ge1$. Torsion-free means that no nonzero stalk element is annihilated by a nonzero local function. Suppose it has a framing, namely an isomorphism $\phi:\mathcal E|_{L_\infty}\xrightarrow{\sim}W\otimes\mathcal O_{L_\infty}$ for $W=\mathbb C^N$, and Hilbert polynomial $\chi(\mathcal E(m))=N\binom{m+2}{2}-k$ for $k\ge0$, where $\chi$ is the alternating sum of coherent-sheaf cohomology dimensions. Then $\mathcal E$ is locally free near $L_\infty$ and

$$H^0(\mathcal E(-1))=H^0(\mathcal E(-2))=H^2(\mathcal E(-1))=H^2(\mathcal E(-2))=0.$$

$$\dim H^1(\mathcal E(-1))=\dim H^1(\mathcal E(-2))=k,\qquad H^0(\mathcal E\otimes\Omega^1)=H^2(\mathcal E\otimes\Omega^1)=0,\qquad \dim H^1(\mathcal E\otimes\Omega^1)=2k+N.$$
The diagonal on $\mathbb P^2\times\mathbb P^2$ has its length-two Koszul resolution from the regular rank-two section described in the proof. Its associated finite Beilinson hypercohomology complex, applied to $\mathcal E(-1)$ and twisted by $\mathcal O(1)$, is a monad

$$H^1(\mathcal E(-2))\otimes\mathcal O(-1)\longrightarrow H^1(\mathcal E\otimes\Omega^1)\otimes\mathcal O\longrightarrow H^1(\mathcal E(-1))\otimes\mathcal O(1)$$

whose only cohomology is $\mathcal E$ in the middle. For an algebraic family over a finite-type complex base, the same construction is a family of monads provided the sheaf is flat over the base, the displayed cohomology groups have the stated constant ranks, and the corresponding cohomology-and-base-change maps are isomorphisms.

source_changes.old_Statement:
Assume AC. Let $V=\mathbb C^k$, $W=\mathbb C^N$, $N\ge1$, $k\ge0$, and let $(B_1,B_2,I,J)$ satisfy $[B_1,B_2]+IJ=0$ and be stable, meaning that the vectors obtained by applying all words in $B_1,B_2$ to $I(W)$ span $V$. Costable means that no nonzero common $B_1,B_2$-invariant subspace lies in $\ker J$, and regular means stable and costable. On $\mathbb P^2$ with coordinates $[z_0:z_1:z_2]$, define

$$\alpha=\begin{pmatrix}z_0B_1-z_1\\z_0B_2-z_2\\z_0J\end{pmatrix}:V\otimes\mathcal O(-1)\to(V\oplus V\oplus W)\otimes\mathcal O,\qquad \beta=\begin{pmatrix}-z_0B_2+z_2&z_0B_1-z_1&z_0I\end{pmatrix}:(V\oplus V\oplus W)\otimes\mathcal O\to V\otimes\mathcal O(1).$$

Then $\beta\alpha=z_0^2([B_1,B_2]+IJ)=0$, $\alpha$ is injective as a sheaf map, and $\beta$ is surjective at every point. The three-term complex is a monad, meaning it is exact at its first and last terms; its middle cohomology $\mathcal E=\ker\beta/\operatorname{im}\alpha$ is torsion-free of rank $N$, has Hilbert polynomial $N\binom{m+2}{2}-k$, and has a canonical framing $\mathcal E|_{L_\infty}\cong W\otimes\mathcal O_{L_\infty}$. Every framed torsion-free sheaf with this rank, framing and Hilbert polynomial arises uniquely up to simultaneous change of basis in $V$ from this construction. For a finite-type complex scheme $S$, a family of ADHM data is a rank-$k$ vector bundle with endomorphisms and framing maps satisfying the equation and stable on every geometric fiber; its monad cohomology is flat over $S$, and the two constructions are inverse on those families for which the relative cohomology bundles and base-change maps in the preceding Beilinson lemma have the stated ranks and are isomorphisms. A first-order framed deformation means an isomorphism class of such a family over $\mathbb C[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)$ with its special fiber identified; the correspondence induces inverse maps on those deformation spaces and their tangent vector spaces. The sheaf is locally free exactly when the ADHM datum is costable; hence the regular locus is the locally-free sheaf locus. Combined with the real/complex quotient theorem, positive-FI data correspond to all such framed torsion-free sheaves, while the zero-FI real quotient corresponds to the locally-free locus. The framing representation has character $\sum_{a=1}^N e_a^{-1}$ and the dual framing has character $\sum_{a=1}^N e_a$.

source_changes.old_Statement: Assume full AC and DC. Let $Z=\mathbb C\mathbb P^3$, let $G=\operatorname{Gr}(2,4)$ be the complex Grassmannian of projective lines in $Z$, and let $p:\mathscr L\to G$ be the universal line family with evaluation map $e:\mathscr L\to Z$. Let $\mathcal E\to Z$ be a holomorphic rank-$N$ bundle, $N\geq2$, with a positive Hermitian real structure and a unitary framing on the twistor line at $\infty$. Assume its restriction to every real twistor line $L_x$ is holomorphically and unitarily trivial. The degree-zero base-change maps at every real line are isomorphisms. Then $(p_*e^*\mathcal E)|_{S^4}$ is a smooth Hermitian rank-$N$ vector bundle, its fibre at $x$ is $H^0(L_x,\mathcal E|_{L_x})$, and the evaluation morphism identifies its pullback to the real incidence family with $e^*\mathcal E$. More precisely, for every real line, there is a complex-open neighbourhood in $G$ on whose entire universal-line family the evaluation morphism is an isomorphism. The framing on $L_\infty$ induces a unitary framing of this bundle at $\infty$.

source_changes.old_Statement:
Assume full AC and the exact projective GAGA comparison used below; its substantial local analytic prerequisites remain unresolved in its own carrier. The local smooth integrable-Dolbeault frame theorem is supplied by the explicit local proof, rather than assumed as a new analytic input.

For $N\geq2$, let $\mathcal M^{\mathrm{ASD}}_{k,N}$ be the framed unitary ASD sector on the round oriented $S^4$ defined above. On the Ward side take a holomorphic rank-$N$ bundle $\mathcal E$ on $Z$, a positive Hermitian Ward reality datum, and a unitary framing on $L_\infty$. Require $\mathcal E|_{L_x}\cong\mathcal O_{L_x}^{\oplus N}$ for every real twistor line, and require $c_2(\mathcal E)=kH^2$, where $H=c_1(\mathcal O_Z(1))$. Then $\widehat E_x=H^0(L_x,\mathcal E|_{L_x})$ forms a smooth rank-$N$ Hermitian bundle on $S^4$. For each section of $\widehat E_x$, extend it holomorphically and uniquely to the first infinitesimal neighbourhood of $L_x$ and differentiate this extension in the family of lines; this defines the Ward connection $\widehat\nabla$. The form induced by the positive holomorphic reality pairing is smooth and is preserved by $\widehat\nabla$; this is a conclusion, not an independent metric-compatibility assumption.

Under these hypotheses, the Ward construction gives a bijection between based unitary gauge classes in $\mathcal M^{\mathrm{ASD}}_{k,N}$ and isomorphism classes of the specified framed Ward bundles. The reconstructed Ward connection satisfies $F^+=0$ and $q_N=-k$. The inverse sends a framed ASD connection to the holomorphic structure on $\pi^*E$ whose vertical part is the standard Dolbeault operator and whose horizontal $(0,1)$ part is the connection on the planes $\ell\otimes S_x^-$. Both maps preserve the framing, Hermitian form, charge, and compact torus action. Reducible bundles and flat summands are included; no irreducibility assumption is imposed.

Let $A$ be a smooth framed anti-self-dual unitary connection on the specified round oriented $S^4$, and let $\mathcal E$ be its holomorphic Ward bundle on $Z=\mathbb C\mathbb P^3$. Suppose the following conditional Penrose-transform input is supplied for both $\mathcal E$ and its dual $\mathcal E^\vee$: there are injective linear maps

$$\mathcal P_{\mathcal E}:H^1(Z,\mathcal E(-2))\longrightarrow\{s\in\Gamma(E):(\nabla_A^*\nabla_A+R/6)s=0\},$$

and the analogous map for $\mathcal E^\vee$, where $R>0$ is the scalar curvature of the round metric and the target connection is the induced unitary connection. Then

$$H^1(Z,\mathcal E(-2))=H^1(Z,\mathcal E^\vee(-2))=0.$$

This is a conditional vanishing result; it does not assert or prove the Penrose-transform input.

Let $A$ be a framed unitary ASD connection on the round oriented $S^4$, let $\mathcal E$ be its Ward bundle on $Z=\mathbb CP^3$, and let $k=-q_N(A)$. Use the exact coupled cohomology-vanishing input stated below for both $\mathcal E$ and $\mathcal E^\vee$. Assume also the exact projective GAGA and line-family base-change inputs needed to regard $\mathcal E$ as an algebraic bundle, to make its restrictions trivial on a complex-open neighbourhood of at least one real twistor line, and to apply the diagonal resolution. Finally, use the Chern-character normalization $\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal E)=N-kH^2$ in $A^*(\mathbb CP^3)_\mathbb Q$, where $H=c_1(\mathcal O(1))$; this normalization is conditional on the twistor pullback class convention matching the framed charge.

Under these inputs,

$$H^1(Z,\mathcal E(-2))=H^1(Z,\mathcal E^\vee(-2))=0.$$

There is a canonical Beilinson three-term monad

$$\mathcal O_Z(-1)\otimes U\longrightarrow\mathcal O_Z\otimes K\longrightarrow\mathcal O_Z(1)\otimes U',$$

whose middle cohomology is $\mathcal E$ and whose terms are

$$U=H^2(Z,\mathcal E(-3)),\qquad K=H^2(Z,\mathcal E\otimes\Omega_Z^2),\qquad U'=H^2(Z,\mathcal E\otimes\Omega_Z^1(-1)),$$

with $\dim U=\dim U'=k$ and $\dim K=2k+N$. The construction is natural in framed bundle isomorphisms and unique up to changes of bases in $U,K,U'$. The values of all global parallel sections form its maximal trivial flat parallel summand, and the connection splits orthogonally into that summand and a summand with no nonzero parallel sections; arbitrary nonflat parallel summands are permitted. The monad construction is additive across this splitting and uses no hypothesis $H^0(Z,\mathcal E)=0$.

Let $N\geq2$, $k\geq0$, and let a framed real Ward bundle on $Z=\mathbb CP^3$ have the normalized linear monad with vector-space dimensions $k,2k+N,k$. Then the real monad is equivalent to a raw datum $(B_1,B_2,I,J)$ on $V=\mathbb C^k$, $W=\mathbb C^N$ in exactly the convention

$$\mu_{\mathbb C}=[B_1,B_2]+IJ=0,\qquad \mu_{\mathbb R}=[B_1,B_1^\dagger]+[B_2,B_2^\dagger]+II^\dagger-J^\dagger J=0.$$

source_changes.old_Statement:
Assume AC and the exact rank-two regular zero-FI ADHM/ASD correspondence, with all its actual analytic and intrinsic normal-form prerequisites. Fix $k\ge0$, $V=\mathbb C^k$ and $W=\mathbb C$. Let $\mathcal A^{\mathrm{reg}}_{k,1}$ be the orbit set by $U(V)$ of $B_1,B_2\in\operatorname{End}(V)$, $I:W\to V$, $J:V\to W$ with

$$[B_1,B_2]+IJ=0,\qquad [B_1,B_1^\dagger]+[B_2,B_2^\dagger]+II^\dagger-J^\dagger J=0,$$

such that words in the $B_i$ applied to $I(W)$ span $V$ and no nonzero common invariant subspace lies in $\ker J$. On the positively stereographically oriented unit round $S^4$, let $\mathcal M^{\mathrm{ASD}}_{k,1}$ be the set of smooth Hermitian line bundles $L$, smooth unitary connections $A$ with $F_A^+=0$, and unitary framings $\Phi:L_\infty\to\mathbb C$, with $q_1=-(8\pi^2)^{-1}\int F_A\wedge F_A=-k$, modulo framed unitary isomorphisms. After a fixed framed bundle is chosen, its gauge group consists of smooth unitary automorphisms equal to identity at infinity.

The regular complex $GL(V)$ quotient, defined by retaining the complex equation and the same stability and costability, has the same empty-or-point classification under the zero-FI real/complex quotient identification. For $k>0$ both ordinary sets are empty. For $k=0$ they are the single empty raw datum and the framed flat line, respectively, with no framed stabilizer. This identification is equivariant for $T=(S^1)^2\times S^1$, with $h=e^{-1}$, raw action $(t_1B_1,t_2B_2,Ih^{-1},t_1t_2hJ)$ and connection action by inverse rotational pullback and postcomposition of the framing with $h$; on the resulting point these actions are trivial.

A first-order real Hermitian family here is over $D=\mathbb C[\varepsilon]/(\varepsilon^2)$ with involution $\varepsilon^\dagger=\varepsilon$. On the raw side use free $D$-modules of ranks $k,1$, the displayed equations over $D$, regular reduction, fixed framing module, and unitary $D$-linear changes of basis. On the connection side use locally free smooth Hermitian line-bundle deformations with framed special fiber and a unitary connection $A_0+\varepsilon a$, satisfying ASD coefficientwise, modulo unitary gauge transformations with framed reduction and value identity at infinity. For $k>0$ these groupoids are empty; for $k=0$ each is equivalent to the one-object groupoid with trivial automorphism group. The identification commutes with reduction, infinitesimal scalar base changes preserving the involution, and the compact action. In particular it identifies their zero tangent spaces and restricts to the exact locally-free/base-change family range in the rank-two correspondence.
